title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Benefits
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare, saying your benefits will be canceled unless you give them personal information or pay a fee. They may sound urgent and try to scare you.
example_message: "This is Medicare. We need to verify your Social Security number or your coverage will be canceled immediately. Please give us your number now."
red_flags: Caller says your benefits will be canceled right away
They ask for your Social Security or bank information
They pressure you to act quickly
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have questions.

title: Fake Tech Support Pop-Ups on Your Computer
how_it_works: A pop-up appears on your computer warning of a virus or problem, and tells you to call a number for help. The person on the phone asks for remote access or payment to 'fix' your computer.
example_message: "Warning! Your computer is infected. Call Microsoft Support now at 1-888-XXX-XXXX to fix the issue."
red_flags: Unsolicited pop-up with a phone number
Urgent language about viruses or hacking
They ask to control your computer or want payment
what_to_do: Close the pop-up and do not call the number; if you’re worried, ask a trusted friend or local computer shop for help.

title: Grandparent Emergency Scam
how_it_works: Someone calls pretending to be your grandchild or a lawyer, saying your grandchild is in trouble and needs money right away. They may ask you not to tell anyone.
example_message: "Grandma, it's me. I’m in trouble and need you to send money for bail. Please don’t tell Mom or Dad."
red_flags: Caller claims to be a relative in trouble
They want money sent fast, often by gift card or wire
They say to keep it a secret
what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or another family member directly to check.

title: Social Security Text Message Scam
how_it_works: You get a text saying there’s a problem with your Social Security account. The message has a link or phone number and asks you to confirm your information.
example_message: "Your Social Security account is suspended. Click here to reactivate: [fake link]"
red_flags: Message asks you to click a link or call a number
Requests for personal or financial information
what_to_do: Delete the message and do not click any links or call the number.

title: Romance Scam on Social Media
how_it_works: A scammer pretends to be interested in a relationship online. After gaining your trust, they ask for money for an emergency or travel.
example_message: "I care about you so much, but I need help with a sudden medical bill. Can you send me some money?"
red_flags: Online friend quickly expresses love or affection
They ask for money, often for an emergency
They avoid meeting in person or video chatting
what_to_do: Never send money to someone you haven’t met in person, no matter how convincing they seem.
